title.narrative: Learning for Diversity: culture and education together

description.narrative: Culture and education are fundamental to human development, community wellbeing and the building of adaptive, innovative, pluralistic and peaceful societies. Together, they have the potential to expand educational trajectories, empowering communities and people with the necessary skills and tools to live together in peace and inspire positive change. To achieve the Education 2030 Agenda, in all its dimensions, and advance all Sustainable Development Goals, it is necessary to adopt an interdisciplinary, intersectoral approach to ensure that education systems equip learners with the knowledge, skills, attitudes, values and behaviours they need to flourish as individuals and contribute to the building of inclusive, peaceful and sustainable societies. In today's increasingly multicultural societies, this implies contextualizing educational content and methods, to ensure content and context-relevance, and making a concerted effort in favour of quality education in line with SDG 4 so as to ensure education contributes to eradicating poverty, curbing discrimination and prejudice. Further, culturally grounded education can promote dialogue fostering respect for cultural diversity, global citizenship, education for sustainable development, and promoting dialogue and peace from a human rights-based perspective, inter alia, by complementing and renewing conventional educational approaches and pedagogies, linking formal, non-formal and informal learning and expanding learners' skills and capacities notably through TVET and digital technologies. Despite its transformative potential, culture is insufficiently integrated and mobilized in learning processes, contents, pedagogies, and ultimately as an enriching foundation and resource for learning that would ensure inclusive, content- and context-relevant and equitable quality education and lifelong learning for all. Relatedly, education serves as a powerful vehicle for knowledge across the diverse dimensions of culture, from heritage to arts and creativity, contributing to social transformation and supporting future generations and informed citizens in adapting to contemporary challenges. Through encompassing culture, creativity, and critical thinking education can promote employment generation for creative economy, skills development, cultural heritage safeguarding and upholding the positive force of cultural diversity to broaden opportunities for sustainable development in line with the shaping of the Pact for the Future and of UNESCO’s advocacy for the inclusion of culture as a standalone goal in the post-2030 sustainable development prospects. Against this backdrop, UNESCO is committed to mobilize a reinvestment in culture and arts education to address the challenges of a fast-evolving landscape calling for more robust, agile, and resilient knowledge societies equipped with the necessary critical and professional skills and capacities to adapt to the evolving priorities and needs, and to support active and engaged citizens. In this aim, a revision process towards a new Framework for Culture and Arts Education is instrumental with the aim of expanding the existing UNESCO frameworks on arts education (the Lisbon Roadmap and the Seoul Agenda) to integrate the various dimensions of culture, from heritage to creativity, cultural activities, and cultural institutions - taking into consideration the digital transformation and artificial intelligence, along with their influence on both education and culture.
